evals.prompt: Using the Blackwork version already installed in this Next.js project, build a bilingual project-list page with site chrome, project cards, tags, and icon-only links to the homepage and repository.
evals.expected_output: A restrained content composition that uses the installed Blackwork API, keeps repeated cards aligned, and exposes accessible icon actions.
expectations: Inspects the installed Blackwork version or declarations before choosing imports
Uses one page title and compact card titles rather than repeating hero-sized headings
Uses consistent Card slots for repeated projects without nesting cards
Provides accessible names and tooltips or equivalent discoverable labels for icon-only links
Checks long translated text and wrapping at a mobile viewport
Uses semantic theme colors for page chrome

evals.prompt: Build a Blackwork-based poster generator with image, layout, and background settings; a live fixed-ratio preview; export-size selection; and an export action. It must work on desktop, mobile, light, and dark themes.
evals.expected_output: A stable workbench with grouped settings, a dominant preview, explicit mobile ordering, intentional canvas theme independence, and visual verification.
expectations: Uses a narrower settings region and wider preview region on desktop
Defines an intentional mobile order instead of clipping the desktop grid
Constrains the preview with aspect ratio and local overflow so it cannot widen the page
Keeps exported canvas colors independent from semantic application chrome
Keeps export controls stable while preview or loading content changes
Verifies representative desktop and mobile viewports in both themes

evals.prompt: Review and fix a cramped Blackwork toolbar where the page title duplicates a panel title, copy/reset/download icons have no labels, gaps are inconsistent, and the light canvas looks accidental in dark mode.
evals.expected_output: A focused correction that restores hierarchy, groups tools, adds accessible tooltips, and deliberately frames the domain canvas without forcing it to follow the app theme.
expectations: Removes or demotes the redundant title instead of keeping competing headings
Uses consistent square icon actions with accessible names and tooltips
Groups related actions with a small spacing rhythm and separates the primary action
Frames a deliberately light canvas clearly inside semantic dark application chrome
Does not propose a wholesale redesign when focused composition changes solve the defects
